subject: Integration discovery: routing policy, SDK auth & reranker POC
messages:

Subject: Follow-up + architecture notes from today's discovery

Thanks for the call earlier — this was super helpful. A few follow-ups from our side as we scope a small POC: 

- We need a short writeup on the simplest SDK/auth approach for our engineers (we currently use Okta for service accounts).
- Clarify how model routing would look for a mixed workload: low-latency chat (EU users), cheaper batch embeddings (US), and a reranker step for search relevance.
- Any recommendations on structured outputs / tool-calling for our document ingestion pipeline (we want consistent JSON outputs for downstream indexers).

I've attached a quick diagram of our current edge + ingestion flow (current_arch.png). Also: procurement will want an estimate of how long a sandbox POC would take and a draft SOW.

Would appreciate a concise list of next steps and who from your side should be involved.

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 17:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up + architecture notes from today's discovery

Thanks Marta — great questions. Recap + proposed next steps below. I'm copying Ben (AE) and Laura (SE) so we can coordinate a technical deep-dive and commercial timeline.

Recap of constraints you mentioned:
- EU-first low-latency conversational endpoint for clinicians (99th pctl latency target ~200ms).
- US batch embeddings for nightly index refresh (cost sensitivity).
- Reranker step after candidate generation to improve relevance; must be deterministic and reproducible for A/B.
- Okta-backed identity for service accounts and corporate SSO for admin UI.

High-level proposal (POC scope):
1) Sandbox with two pinned model routes: inbox-chat-eu (low-latency, FP16 quantized variant) + embeddings-us (throughput-optimized variant).
2) Add a lightweight rerank route that calls an embeddings endpoint + small cross-encoder for final scoring (we can host reranker as a separate route).
3) Routing policy: region-pin -> latency-first with cost-fallback. Default: route by region tag; if latency SLO violated, failover to next compatible variant (same model family but higher perf).
4) SDK/auth: we support short-lived service tokens via Okta-issued JWTs (service account flow) or API keys scoped to routes. For the POC we recommend JWT + role-based scopes for least privilege.
5) Structured output/tool calling: use Redwood's structured output schema (we'll include an example) + a tool calling layer for external indexer calls to guarantee JSON contract.

Immediate next steps: 
- Laura: schedule a 60m deep-dive next week to walk through SDK + sample policy.
- Ben: align on commercial timeline and provide an initial sandbox offer + high-level SOW.
- Tessa (me): share a short playbook draft and an example route-policy JSON.

Attachments: redwood-playbook-draft.pdf (high-level POC plan), route-policy-example.json (sample routing policy).

If that aligns, Marta — can you confirm ideal POC start week and three technical attendees for next week's deep-dive?

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Partner
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:16:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Follow-up + architecture notes from today's discovery

Marta — quick technical follow-up from my side with concrete steps you can hand to engineering.

SDK & auth (recommended POC):
1) Service account (Okta) issues a JWT for an integration identity. Redwood accepts JWTs with a standard claim set (iss, sub, aud, exp) and validates via your Okta keys.
2) Example header (HTTP):
   Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGci...
3) We recommend scoping the token to routes via claims: routes:["inbox-chat-eu","reranker-eu","embeddings-us"]

Client setup:
- Install our language SDK (pip/npm) and set a single environment variable REDWOOD_AUTH=BearerJWT
- Sample CLI to run a quick ping: redwoodctl ping --route inbox-chat-eu

Routing/policy details (example, placed here as plaintext for copy/paste):
{
  "policy_name": "eu-latency-primary-cost-fallback",
  "rules": [
    {"match": {"region": "eu"}, "action": "route", "route": "inbox-chat-eu"},
    {"match": {"latency_ms_gt": 250}, "action": "fallback", "route": "inbox-chat-eu-highperf"},
    {"match": {"cost_per_token_gt": 0.002}, "action": "route", "route": "inbox-chat-eu-cheap"}
  ]
}

Notes on reranker: keep candidate generation and reranker as separate calls to enforce reproducibility. Reranker should be deterministic (no sampling). We recommend model checksum/version pinning in the route config to avoid silent regressions.

Attachments: route-policy-example.json (JSON file with the above example + variations).

I'll bring a runnable sample policy + handshake script to the deep-dive so your engineers can run it in a sandbox without changing prod infra.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
